title: Cover letter data
description: The cover letter's source. build/build_letter.py renders it as a single flowing column — no measurement pass, no layout solver. Building it never touches the resume's files.

name.description: Your name, split in two so the design can weight them differently. Same shape as the resume's. Optional here: if data/_profile.yml supplies it, omit it and this file inherits it.

role.description: Optional subtitle under your name — usually the role this letter is for.

contact.description: Contact details in the letterhead. Normally omitted here and inherited from data/_profile.yml, which is the same file the resume inherits from — that is how the two documents stay in sync.

rows.description: Clickable contact lines. Use an empty list for address only.

meta.description: Optional document metadata. Only these two fields are read.

description.description: One sentence, stamped into the PDF's metadata.

recipient.description: The address block — name, company, street, city. Two forms, both accepted: a list of strings (one per line), or a single block scalar written with '|', which you can paste an address straight into. Unlike body, this splits on EVERY line, not on blank ones: each line is its own entry.

oneOf.description: One block of text; each non-empty line becomes an entry.

body.description: The whole letter, greeting and sign-off included. Two forms, both accepted: a list of strings (one per paragraph), or a single block scalar written with '|' where blank lines separate paragraphs. The block form is easier to paste into and easier to read. Start with 'Dear …,' and end with 'Sincerely,' — they are paragraphs like any other; the typed name below them is added from your profile.

oneOf.description: One block of text; blank lines split it into paragraphs.
